subject.title: Feature: Include trusted sender_name in inbound metadata envelope

question: Should OpenClaw expose a human-readable sender display name as trusted system metadata, or keep trusted metadata limited to stable identifiers/canonical principals and leave display names in untrusted context?
rationale: Current main intentionally excludes sender names from trusted prompt metadata, while the issue asks to move identity into the trusted envelope and related PRs propose incompatible trust boundaries.

options.title: Use canonical principal metadata
options.body: Treat identityLinks or SourceActor-style stable principal metadata as the trusted contract, and keep display names in untrusted context unless separately attested.

options.title: Add trusted sender display name
options.body: Allow a `sender_name`/`sender_display_name` trusted field only from explicitly verified channel or operator provenance, with privacy and spoofing tests.

options.title: Defer until related PRs converge
options.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers choose between the open provenance, Discord identity-links, SourceActor, and chat.send author proposals.

recommendation.title: Use canonical principal metadata
recommendation.body: Treat identityLinks or SourceActor-style stable principal metadata as the trusted contract, and keep display names in untrusted context unless separately attested.

likelyOwner.reason: The current boundary and the most recent broad refactor of this path are tied to steipete, and the remaining choice spans core prompt/security policy.
